# 242 — PR explainer

*Read top to bottom; the diff is described in reading order at the end.*

*Tier: HIGH, as the spec's own risk tier called it — a generated SEO surface at estate scale
(2,102 pages, freshly measured) plus a shared-module move `generate-spotlight.js` depends on.*

---

## The goal

Item 229 built a rule: a headline yield figure may not be shown as a recommendation unless it is
checked against that pool's own recent (30-day) average rate. 229 enforced that rule at exactly
one of the four ranked surfaces this repo emits — the X-spotlight packs. This item enforces the
same rule, using the exact same code, at the highest-traffic of the remaining three surfaces: the
2,102 static `/tokens/<symbol>` pages that exist specifically to be crawled and cited.

Before this item, a token page's headline rate was `Math.max(...rec.pools.map(poolTotalApy))` —
literally "the single most extreme number on the page" — with zero check against whether that
number was a fluke. Worse, a second, independent bug sat right next to it: the page attributed
that headline rate to `rec.pools[0]`, the pool with the most TVL, which is very often a
*different pool* than the one that actually earns the headline rate. So the page could say "the
highest yield is 694.11% on Protocol A" when Protocol A's own pool pays 20%, and the 694% actually
belongs to some other, unrelated pool the reader is never told about.

## The intuition

One sentence: **a headline number and the name printed next to it must always come from the same
pool.**

Today's code violates this in a way that's easy to miss reading either line in isolation:

```js
const bestApy = Math.max(...rec.pools.map(poolTotalApy));   // the pool with the highest rate
const top = rec.pools[0];                                    // the pool with the most TVL
buildAnswerAndFaq(rec.symbol, rec, bestApy, top, language);  // rate from ONE pool, name from ANOTHER
```

Neither line is wrong on its own — `bestApy` genuinely is the max, `top` genuinely is the
TVL leader. The bug only exists in the GAP between them: nothing ties the two together. On
19.8% of pages (measured; 20.0% re-measured today) they happen to be different pools, and the
page states a rate no protocol named on the page actually pays.

229 already solved half of this — `isRepresentativeRate(pool)` answers "is this pool's current
rate close to its own history, or is it a fluke?" — but 229 only wired that check into the
spotlight packs. This item's whole job is: **pick ONE pool** (the highest-rate pool that also
passes the representativeness check), and use that SAME pool for both the number and the name.
That single selection function is `headlinePoolFor(pools)`.

## Why the code has to move first

`isRepresentativeRate` and its three supporting pieces (`REPRESENTATIVE_REL`,
`REPRESENTATIVE_ABS_PP`, `representativenessRatio`) lived in `generate-spotlight.js`. Their only
real dependency is `poolTotalApy`, which lives in `generate-token-pages.js`. Two structural facts
force the move to go this direction and not the other:

1. `generate-spotlight.js` already does `require('./generate-token-pages.js')` — so if
   `generate-token-pages.js` tried to `require('./generate-spotlight.js')` back, that's a CommonJS
   require cycle.
2. `generate-spotlight.js` also hard-requires `@napi-rs/canvas` (for its share-card PNG renderer)
   — a real, heavyweight native dependency that has no reason to load just to check whether a rate
   is representative. Pulling it into the token-page generator would put the entire SEO build
   pipeline at the mercy of a canvas library it doesn't use.

So the four names move INTO `generate-token-pages.js` (where `poolTotalApy` already lives), and
`generate-spotlight.js` imports them back — same names, same values, one implementation, checked
by a test that literally asserts both modules point at the identical function objects.

## What changed and why

**1. Moved, not duplicated.** `REPRESENTATIVE_REL`, `REPRESENTATIVE_ABS_PP`,
`representativenessRatio(pool)`, `isRepresentativeRate(pool)` now live in
`generate-token-pages.js`. `generate-spotlight.js` imports all four from its existing
`require('./generate-token-pages.js')` line and re-exports them under the same names — every
existing spotlight test and caller (`pickPool`, `storySignals`) is unaffected, because they
never cared where the names came from, only that they resolve.

**2. One pool, one claim.** New function:

```js
function headlinePoolFor(pools) {
  // among pools, the highest-poolTotalApy pool that ALSO passes isRepresentativeRate;
  // if none pass, the highest-poolTotalApy pool anyway (documented, honest fallback)
}
```

**3. Both twins call it identically.** `renderTokenPage` and `renderTokenPageMarkdown` each now
do:
```js
const headlinePool = headlinePoolFor(rec.pools);
const bestApy = poolTotalApy(headlinePool);
buildAnswerAndFaq(rec.symbol, rec, bestApy, headlinePool, language);  // same pool, both args
```
`top = rec.pools[0]` is untouched — it still feeds `tcpTokenIntro`'s "here's your token's biggest
pool" sentence, with its own honest APY. That line was never wrong; it just isn't the headline.

## What did NOT change

The visible pool table (still every pool, TVL-sorted, unchanged order — proven by a test), which
tokens get a page at all (`rankTopTokens`'s gates untouched), the sitemap, the yield-headline
KPI line, every trust rail (`APY_SANITY_LIMIT`, `MIN_POOL_TVL`, anomaly exclusion), and the entire
chain-page estate (`generate-chain-pages.js` has the IDENTICAL `Math.max`/`rec.pools[0]` bug —
explicitly left open, filed as item 243, not touched here).

## The diff, in reading order

1. **`generate-token-pages.js`, right after `poolTotalApy`**: the four moved
   constants/functions land here, doc comments intact, with a note explaining the move.
2. **`generate-token-pages.js`, before `buildAnswerAndFaq`**: `headlinePoolFor(pools)`.
3. **`generate-token-pages.js`, `renderTokenPage`**: `bestApy`/`buildAnswerAndFaq`'s 4th arg
   switch from `Math.max(...)`/`top` to `headlinePoolFor(rec.pools)`'s result.
4. **`generate-token-pages.js`, `renderTokenPageMarkdown`**: the identical change, so the two
   twins can never state different numbers for the same page.
5. **`generate-token-pages.js`, `module.exports`**: the four moved names plus `headlinePoolFor`
   added to the export list.
6. **`generate-spotlight.js`, the require line**: extended to pull in the four moved names.
7. **`generate-spotlight.js`, the old definitions**: deleted, replaced by a comment pointing at
   step 1. `module.exports` keeps re-exporting all four (see Deviations — one of the four,
   `representativenessRatio`, was never actually exported before; it is now, matching the spec's
   literal instruction to re-export "all four").
8. **`test_token_pages.js`**: a new `242 —` block — a fixture population run through the real
   `rankTopTokens`, checked for the headline-APY invariant, the attribution invariant (project AND
   chain match the headline pool, in both the answer block and FAQ A1, EN and KO), markdown-twin
   parity, two positive controls lifted from the spec's own worked numbers, an unchanged-table-
   order proof, and a mirror-identity proof with an honest fallback for environments missing
   `@napi-rs/canvas`.

## Deviations worth knowing about (full detail in `242-notes.md`)

- `generate-spotlight.js` gained one export it never had (`representativenessRatio`) — the spec
  asks for all four names to be re-exported identically, and only three of the four were being
  exported pre-242.
- `@napi-rs/canvas` was actually installable in this build session (the spec assumed it wasn't) —
  this is recorded in detail in the notes, along with a standalone proof that the test's
  "package missing" fallback branch still works correctly when the package genuinely isn't there.
- The re-measured live numbers (fresh fetch, same day) land within a point or two of the spec's
  own numbers — expected, since the live pool set moves continuously.

## Quiz

1. Why does `generate-token-pages.js` import from nowhere related to `generate-spotlight.js`, but
   `generate-spotlight.js` imports from `generate-token-pages.js`, and not the other way around?
2. `headlinePoolFor` has a fallback path. What does it fall back to, and why is that the "smallest
   honest option" rather than, say, showing no headline at all?
3. Two independent bugs are described in this item's evidence: an "unchecked headline" bug and an
   "attribution" bug. Which one did item 229 already partially fix, and which one is new, found
   during this item's own blindspot pass?
4. Why does the acceptance test for the mirror proof need a fallback branch at all — what would
   happen if it just did `require('./generate-spotlight.js')` unconditionally in an environment
   without `@napi-rs/canvas`?
5. `top = rec.pools[0]` still appears in `renderTokenPage`, right next to the new
   `headlinePool` variable. Is this a leftover bug, or intentional — and if intentional, what does
   `top` still get used for?
